# BASE59 PasswordField interaction applicability

Reference source: exact `59ba49768494c1dd54cd8f3a86ca38e745dfb1e5:design-source/auth.dc.html`
bytes copied by git-show, SHA-256
`0a48f029dec14ce30ea4e1b9eed91f275a88a52d418a53f269ab086ce1d996a6`.
Readback matches the immutable base manifest. No browser was launched for this
re-check and no source, style, DOM, Issue or runtime was changed.

## Element-to-selector relationship

The password reveal button is defined directly beside each mkField password
input. The same button occurs at canvas line 110 (password login), line 163
(registration), and line 253 (reset-complete). Every one carries BOTH `data-link`
and the literal inline style `text-underline-offset:4px`:

```html
<button onClick="{{ togglePw }}" type="button" aria-label="{{ pwToggleAria }}" data-link style="text-underline-offset:4px;position:absolute;top:0;right:0;height:100%;padding:0 14px;background:transparent;border:0;cursor:pointer;font:inherit;font-size:12px;font-weight:800;color:{{ linkColor }}">{{ pwToggle }}</button>
```

The canvas line 10 selector is:

```css
[data-link]:active,button[style*="text-underline-offset:4px"]:active{opacity:.8!important}
```

Its FIRST selector matches those three concrete buttons because each carries
`data-link`. No inference from a generic anchor rule or dependence on serialized
inline-style formatting is needed. The inline `text-underline-offset:4px`
applies directly to each button; the offset is visible when its underline is
driven on hover/focus.

## Actual baseline implementation and observations

The immutable baseline primitive `password-field.tsx` line 160 uses:

```tsx
className="absolute inset-y-0 right-0 flex w-20 items-center justify-end pr-3 bg-transparent text-xs font-extrabold text-primary-action hover:underline focus-visible:shadow-focus focus-visible:outline-none"
```

The rendered implementation button has no `data-link` attribute and this class
has neither a 4px underline offset nor the opacity press rule. The actual
baseline browser probes in `baseline/results.json` observed `textUnderlineOffset:
auto` (rest/hover/focus) and `opacity: 1` during REAL pointer-down. Hover underline
and the keyboard focus ring were driven and observed.

Therefore both reported differences are REAL reference mismatches for this
specific password-reveal element: offset auto versus canvas 4px; pressed opacity
1 versus canvas .8. They are not generic-rule assumptions. They pre-exist the
caret fix, and this verifier has not claimed that they were independently approved
or that fixing caret resolves them. The lead owns their disclosure/applicability
and any later routing; no style fix or new task is authored here.
